chartSub: Every trainable rank in Holy, Protection and Retribution, placed at its SpellLevels.SpellLevel. Engraving and Runes carry no level and are excluded.
notes: Ability set = SkillLineAbility rows whose class mask includes Paladin on the class skill lines, plus Engraving (2851) and Runes (2853).
That table has no community column names for build 69876, so its columns were identified from their contents: field 003 = SkillLine, 004 = Spell, 006 = ClassMask, 007 = SupercedesSpell.
Paladin has no rage-style resource: every costed ability reads SpellPower.ManaCost raw, with no /10 conversion.
Paladin has no shapeshift forms (SpellShapeshift is empty for this class), so the filter column reads “Form” rather than “Stance” and stays empty.
Cast times are absent: SpellCastTimes is not among the extracted tables.
No hotfixes are applied. The beta client's DBCache.bin is for build 61916, not 69876, so the overlay matched nothing.

Icons are the client's own: SpellMisc.SpellIconFileDataID resolved through the community listfile to interface/icons/<name>.blp, then fetched from Wowhead's CDN and inlined as data URIs (the Artifact sandbox blocks remote images).
Descriptions are verbatim client strings, so the client's own format tokens ($s1, $o1, $d, $AP) are left unresolved rather than guessed at.

Seal of Command is a Retribution talent (tier 2, spell 20375, single rank), not a trainer ability, so it is absent from this ability list: 20915/20918/20919/20920 carry ClassMask 0 in SkillLineAbility and 20424 has no row there at all.

Holy Light's numbered chain (635…25292, Ranks 1–9) skips Rank 5: spell 1042 (level 30) exists in Spell/SpellLevels but carries ClassMask 0 in SkillLineAbility. Alongside it sits a second, unnumbered set of nine Holy Light spells (19982, 19981, 19980, 19968, 1313348, 1313349, 1313350, 1313352, 1313351, at levels 1, 6, 14, 22, 30, 38, 46, 50, 54) with a real Paladin ClassMask, the same description, no NameSubtext_lang, and no SpellPower row. The extractor groups both sets by name into one family; the unnumbered set sorts first (no parseable rank number), so the family's headline card is one of them rather than Rank 1.

SpellPower.PowerCostPct (percent-of-base-mana costs) isn't read by the extraction script, only flat ManaCost. 24 Paladin abilities cost 0 flat mana but a nonzero percent — e.g. Judgement (20271) actually costs 6% base mana and renders here as free.

Descriptions are resolved by the repo's own tools/tooltip parser, driven by a provider built on this database (tools/foreverdesc). 13,543 of 17,577 described spells resolve; the rest keep their raw string.

Two cosmetic fixes are applied on top, with the untouched string kept as descRaw: this client stores reductions as negative base points, so “Reduces … by -0.5 sec” drops the doubled minus, and trailing .0 decimals are trimmed.

A name can carry several parallel rank ladders (Renew ships two complete 10-rank chains, Mutilate three). Each is listed separately and marked “ladder N of M” rather than concatenated into one false chain.
Abilities costing a percentage of base mana store ManaCost 0 and the real figure in SpellPower.PowerCostPct (Judgement 6%, Multi-Shot 13.9%); those show as “N% base mana”.

The talent tree is the client's modern trait system, not the legacy Talent/TalentTab tables — those still hold the vanilla layout and are vestigial. Positions come from TraitNode.PosX/PosY, rank counts from TraitNodeEntry.MaxRanks, the spell from TraitDefinition, prerequisites from TraitEdge, and per-rank values from TraitDefinitionEffectPoints → CurvePoint. Reading the legacy tables instead costs this class real talents and invents ones the client no longer uses.

A spell's own EffectBasePointsF is only a snapshot of a single rank and is not reliably the first or the last — Toughness stores its rank-5 value, Deflection its rank-1, and Deep Wounds stores 0 while its curve runs 20/40/60. The tooltip's per-rank columns and the description both follow the curve, and the description is re-resolved at whatever rank you select in the calculator.

Three talents across the nine classes carry nonsense grid coordinates in this build (Hunter's Lightning Reflexes and Improved Serpent Sting, Priest's Holy Specialization). They are listed under their tree rather than given an invented position.

A damage or healing range is stored as a base value plus a fractional SpellEffect.Variance rather than the old die-sides pair, so the min and max of a range are base x (1 ∓ variance/2) — Frostbolt rank 1 is base 19, variance 0.105, which is 18 to 20. The repo's parser routed $m and $M to the same call and lowercased the selector, so every range rendered collapsed (“97 to 97”); tools/tooltip now distinguishes them.

Abilities in the Season of Discovery spell id space are excluded. The boundary comes from the data rather than a round number: sorting the era build's class abilities shows a 367,178-wide gap between the classic block (ending at 31018) and the SoD block (398196–469145), with Forever's own content starting far above at 1214168. Forever imported SoD wholesale at identical ids — all 458 Engraving/Runes entries match — so what remains is the classic core plus Forever's own additions. Talents are not filtered: 39 of them sit in the SoD band and several gate non-SoD talents, so removing them would strand those and break prerequisite chains.

A tooltip token written without an effect index, such as Wrack's $t, refers to the first effect. The repo's parser left the index at 0 and then subtracted one, so every bare selector looked up effect −1 and returned nothing — Wrack read “every 0 sec”. Fixed in tools/tooltip, keeping $r's separate meaning (bare $r is the spell's range, not an effect radius). Where a value still reads 0, the client's own effect row is 0.

Abilities carry two different cooldowns and the page shows them separately. RecoveryTime is the spell's own; SpellCooldowns.CategoryRecoveryTime is shared across everything in the same SpellCategories.Category, and the tooltip names the siblings — Mortal Strike's 6s is shared with Bloodthirst and Shield Slam. Across the nine classes 715 abilities use a category cooldown against 227 with their own, so collapsing the two into one number hid the mechanic that governs most of them. Cast times come from SpellCastTimes.Base; a negative base means the cast is the ranged weapon's swing, shown as “ranged weapon speed”.

Some abilities sit on their class's own skill line with ClassMask 0 — not class-restricted rather than belonging to no one — and were invisible until now: Mage Evocation, Hunter Aimed Shot and Lacerate, Paladin Judgement of Command and the missing Holy Light rank, Priest Shadow Word: Death, Warlock Curse of the Elements, Druid Innervate and Omen of Clarity, Shaman Lightning Shield. Most ClassMask 0 rows are not abilities though, so only those that are named, carry a real learn level, are not a talent rank under another guise and are outside the SoD band are included — 92 across the nine classes. The skill lines themselves are resolved by id from masked rows, so a class cannot pick up another's spells where two share a line name (Protection is both Warrior and Paladin; Holy is Paladin and Priest).

Where an ability procs, the tooltip expands SpellAuraOptions.ProcTypeMask bit by bit against the repo's own PROC_FLAG enum, and states outright whether a periodic tick can trigger it — that needs bit 18 DEAL_HARMFUL_PERIODIC or bit 21 DEAL_HELPFUL_PERIODIC. Where there is no SpellAuraOptions row at all the tooltip says so, because that means a flat passive rather than something that triggers. The column is a two-word array and both words are read; the client also stores 0x80000000, which reads as a negative in SQLite and is not named in the enum, so it renders as bit 31 rather than being guessed at — it appears on break-on-damage crowd control such as Frost Nova, Entangling Roots and Chains of Ice.

The proc table distinguishes the three separate periodic bits, because they differ by direction: bit 18 DEAL_HARMFUL_PERIODIC and bit 21 DEAL_HELPFUL_PERIODIC are your own ticks, while bit 19 TAKE_HARMFUL_PERIODIC is a periodic ticking on you. In this build 18 and 21 are set on no ability at all, and 19 on 54 — so a tooltip that said only “periodic” would misread the one case that actually occurs.

Where a spell carries one of the spell attributes the sim names in tools/database/dbc/enums.go, the tooltip lists it — CAN_PROC_FROM_PROCS (21 abilities) and CANT_CRIT (17). A proc that lacks CAN_PROC_FROM_PROCS says so explicitly, since whether an effect can be set off by another proc is not visible in its text: Gnome Eureka! has the flag, Undead Touch of the Grave does not. The client carries 16 attribute words and the repo names flags in only four of them, so nothing beyond those four is guessed at.

A proc's rate limits are shown alongside its chance: SpellAuraOptions.ProcCategoryRecovery is the internal cooldown (292 spells in the database have one; Undead Touch of the Grave is 1s), ProcCharges the number of uses, CumulativeAura the stack cap. Where there is no internal cooldown the tooltip says so, since that is the difference between a proc limited only by its chance and one that is rate-capped. SpellProcsPerMinuteID is set on no spell in this build, so no proc here uses the real-PPM system.
